After more than a decade of never adopting a touch screen in its Mac laptop product line, Apple is finally preparing to launch its first MacBook equipped with a touch screen this October, expected to debut alongside a newly redesigned MacBook Pro, with the new model possibly named MacBook Ultra.

Of course, rumours are still just rumours — but almost all reliable sources agree that the MacBook Pro will support touch functionality later this year. Apple itself has even left some clues in macOS 27: Sidecar touch support, pull-to-refresh functionality, and slightly enlarged menu bar items.

As a 13-inch MacBook Air user, that last point is particularly annoying for me, because what used to fit to the left of the 'notch' can no longer all be squeezed in.

You can call these coincidences, but they really do seem to add up. In any case, here's what the first MacBook with a touch screen is expected to offer.

OLED Display with Dynamic Island

On the display front, the redesigned MacBook Pro will feature a Tandem OLED display, with specifications similar to the iPad Pro — the latter is often hailed as one of the best mobile device displays on the market. Tandem OLED is manufactured by stacking multiple layers of OLED panels, delivering outstanding colour performance, strong contrast, and higher brightness.

There are also indications that the new machine will include a Dynamic Island, smaller than the one on the iPhone, but without Face ID support.

Software Optimisations

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple will add a number of special software optimisations to the first touch-screen MacBook Pro, going beyond what is already in the macOS 27 beta:

"For example, if a user touches a button or interface element, a new type of menu will pop up near the user's finger, offering options better suited to touch operation. The software will also display the most appropriate control combinations based on the user's past usage habits. If the user taps an item on the menu bar at the top of the screen, that group of controls will automatically enlarge for easier finger operation."

M5 Pro and M5 Max Chips

Although initial reports indicated that the new MacBook Pro would be the first to adopt M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, Apple has now decided to skip the release of those two chips and move directly to the M7. In other words, the first-generation 2nm chips will not appear on this redesigned MacBook Pro; the new machine will instead use the existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

This computer will not have a base-model version in the short term, but there are rumours that Apple will launch a base-model redesigned MacBook Pro with the M7 chip as early as next spring.

Slightly Thinner Body

One of the design rumours about the new MacBook Pro is that the body will be slightly thinner and lighter — though exactly how noticeable this will be remains unknown. The previous-generation MacBook Pro already looks and feels fairly thick, so if there's progress in this area, it should be welcomed by users — provided thermal performance isn't sacrificed.

Summary

Overall, the first MacBook Pro with a touch screen looks like an exciting upgrade. However, since Apple raised prices in June due to a memory shortage, the pricing of the new machine will also be adjusted accordingly — so I expect the starting price for the 14-inch model to be around US$2,499, and around US$2,999 for the 16-inch.

Are you looking forward to a MacBook with a touch screen? Will you buy one the moment it launches, or wait a while until the base-model 14-inch version becomes available? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
